Yes. One paper shows that vanilla, standard GNNs can do zero-shot link prediction on unseen knowledge graphs if the graph is first reified into a fixed transferable representation; in that setup, textbook GNNs including GAT, GraphSAGE, and R-GCN transferred from one training KG to 40 inductive link-prediction benchmarks, and the best off-the-shelf GAT matched a dedicated KG foundation model [1].

The key difference is that the transfer mechanism is moved from the architecture into the representation, rather than claiming ordinary GNNs on their usual KG input will generalize automatically [1]. Related papers here discuss specialized KG foundation models for unseen graphs [4] or scalable KG link prediction on large graphs [5], but they do not show standard vanilla GNNs doing zero-shot prediction on unknown KGs in the same way [4,5].
